reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) only reports superconductivity in as-prepared HEA and high-entropy ceramic samples, without any investigation of local ordering, its effect on the density of states, or its impact on electron–phonon coupling. None of the key premises about the role of annealing-induced clustering are supported by the provided passages.
premises: Local ordering/clustering of high electron–phonon coupling elements (e.g., Nb, Ti) can occur in HEAs via annealing.
Such local ordering enhances the local electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
Enhanced local density of states boosts electron–phonon coupling.
Boosted electron–phonon coupling enables Cooper pairing and a measurable superconducting transition.
The baseline disordered state yields no or weak superconductivity, while the locally ordered state shows a higher Tc or enhanced superconducting robustness.
